body: Tentatively slated for 5.3 M1 for investigation

@sbrannen - attached is a small gradle project demonstrating the problem.
[GroovyJUnitFailure.zip](https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/files/2053014/GroovyJUnitFailure.zip)
FWIW, the issue still exists when using Groovy 2.5.0.

The error seems to occur in `org.junit.platform.commons.util.ReflectionUtils.findNestedClasses(Class<?>, Set<Class<?>>)`.

Specifically, we assume the invocation of `java.lang.Class.getDeclaredClasses()` will not throw an exception, but in this particular scenario that invocation indeed throws an exception. 

So we'll likely want to wrap that in a try-catch block.
Though it would likely be a better idea to handle the exceptions at a higher level such as in `org.junit.jupiter.engine.discovery.JavaElementsResolver.resolveChildren(TestDescriptor)`.

issue.title: JupiterTestEngine should log discovery errors instead of aborting the entire test plan

repository.name: junit-framework
repository.description: ✅ The programmer-friendly testing framework for Java and the JVM

issue.body:
## Overview

An error reported in #1436 has made us aware that the entire test plan for JUnit Jupiter aborts whenever certain types of errors occur during the discovery phase. Consequently, a single error (e.g., an invalid class file format) can result in **zero** tests being discovered and executed.

This is, however, unacceptable behavior. The `JupiterTestEngine` should log such errors rather than abort the entire discovery process. Logging such errors allows the test plan to discover and execute as many tests as possible while still informing the user of tests that could not be properly _discovered_.

## Proposal

One possible solution would be to add try-catch blocks to `resolveClass()`, `resolveMethod()`, and `resolveUniqueId()` in `JavaElementsResolver`. These try-catch blocks should log errors and swallow them (unless they are _blacklisted_ exceptions).

## Related Issues

- #1436 

## Deliverables

- [x] Ensure that the `JupiterTestEngine` does not abort the entire discovery process when an exception is encountered.
